the impact of an outfall on benthic metabolism is detectable 750 m far from the point source and that the impact is enhanced during upwelling.

the effects of a sewage outfall in a tropical coastal bay were enhanced during the upwellings, and that the analysis of sedimentary features allowed tracing such impact.

the study of the effects of a sewage outfall in a coastal tropical area and its influence on benthic metabolism, which has not been studied in the area yet.
the effects of anthropogenic activities on coastal areas, and the role that the upwelling phenomena play in the impact of such activities in tropical coastal ecosystems.
the study of the impact of anthropogenic pressure in tropical coastal ecosystems, which is an area that has been poorly studied so far.

in this area, anthropogenic pressures, such as the presence of a submarine outfall and upwelling, may act in synergy to enhance ecosystem degradation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

anthropogenic activities in coastal areas are not the same in tropical and in temperate areas, and that the impact of anthropogenic activities in tropical coastal areas might be amplified by upwelling phenomena.

The main takeaway from our work is that

in tropical areas, marine pollution and upwelling act in synergy and may contribute to the deterioration of coastal areas due to the increase of organic matter and nutrient inputs, the increase of microbial respires and the benthic biodiversity.
